title: Computational analysis of memory consolidation following inhibitory avoidance (IA) training in adult and infant rats: Critical roles of CaMKIIalpha and MeCP2.
authors: Zhang, Yili; Smolen, Paul; Alberini, Cristina M; Baxter, Douglas A; Byrne, John H
one_liner_zh: 该文用微分方程建模大鼠抑制性回避训练后的记忆巩固分子通路，涉及CaMKIIalpha、MeCP2等转录因子调控BDNF表达，但无蛋白质-DNA三维互作建模、无AI或物理模拟方法，仅属信号通路动态模拟，与TF-DNA结合机制课题关联弱。
abstract: Key features of long-term memory (LTM), such as its stability and persistence, are acquired during processes collectively referred to as consolidation. The dynamics of biological changes during consolidation are complex. In adult rodents, consolidation exhibits distinct periods during which the engram is more or less resistant to disruption. Moreover, the ability to consolidate memories differs during developmental periods. Although the molecular mechanisms underlying consolidation are poorly understood, the initial stages rely on interacting signaling pathways that regulate gene expression, including brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II alpha (CaMKIIalpha) dependent feedback loops. We investigated the ways in which these pathways may contribute to developmental and dynamical features of consolidation. A computational model of molecular processes underlying consolidation following inhibitory avoidance (IA) training in rats was developed. Differential equations described the actions of CaMKIIalpha, multiple feedback loops regulating BDNF expression, and several transcription factors including methyl-CpG binding protein 2 (MeCP2), histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2), and SIN3 transcription regulator family member A (Sin3a). This model provides novel explanations for the (apparent) rapid forgetting of infantile memory and the temporal progression of memory consolidation in adults. Simulations predict that dual effects of MeCP2 on the expression of bdnf, and interaction between MeCP2 and CaMKIIalpha, play critical roles in the rapid forgetting of infantile memory and the progress of memory resistance to disruptions. These insights suggest new potential targets of therapy for memory impairment.
abstract_zh: 长期记忆（LTM）的关键特征，如其稳定性和持久性，是在统称为巩固的过程中获得的。巩固期间生物变化的动态过程复杂。在成年啮齿动物中，巩固表现出不同的时期，在这些时期中，记忆痕迹（engram）对干扰的抵抗力有所不同。此外，记忆巩固的能力在发育阶段也有所不同。尽管巩固的分子机制尚不完全清楚，但其初始阶段依赖于调控基因表达的相互作用信号通路，包括脑源性神经营养因子（BDNF）和Ca2+/钙调蛋白依赖性蛋白激酶IIα（CaMKIIalpha）依赖的反馈回路。我们研究了这些通路可能如何促进巩固的发育和动态特征。我们开发了一个计算模型，描述了大鼠抑制性回避（IA）训练后巩固的分子过程。微分方程描述了CaMKIIalpha的作用、调控BDNF表达的多个反馈回路，以及包括甲基-CpG结合蛋白2（MeCP2）、组蛋白去乙酰化酶2（HDAC2）和SIN3转录调节家族成员A（Sin3a）在内的几种转录因子。该模型为婴儿期记忆的（明显）快速遗忘和成年期记忆巩固的时间进程提供了新的解释。模拟预测，MeCP2对bdnf表达的双重效应，以及MeCP2与CaMKIIalpha之间的相互作用，在婴儿期记忆的快速遗忘和记忆对干扰抵抗力的进展中起关键作用。这些见解提示了记忆障碍治疗的新潜在靶点。
